choices.text: Every molecule moves faster than before
The average speed rises, but some molecules are still slow
All the molecules move at one identical speed

questions.feedback: If you picked the first choice, that is the trap: In a hotter gas every molecule moves faster. Reteach point: Hotter means a higher average: the whole spread of speeds shifts up, but some molecules still crawl. Heating shifts the average up - it does not give every molecule the same boost.
questions.misconception: In a hotter gas every molecule moves faster.
questions.prompt: A gas is heated from 300 K to 600 K. Which statement is correct?

questions.answer: Conduction: vibrations and free electrons pass kinetic energy from particle to particle along the spoon, from the hot end to the handle.
questions.feedback: The mechanism is conduction - energy relayed particle by particle through a solid, with free electrons doing most of the carrying in a metal. If you wrote convection, remember convection needs a flowing fluid.
questions.prompt: A metal spoon stands in a bowl of hot soup. After a few minutes the top of the handle feels warm. Name the transfer mechanism and explain it in one sentence.

choices.text: It expands, becomes less dense than the cooler water, and is pushed up
It becomes heavier as it warms and sinks upward
The heater blows it upward with radiated packets

questions.feedback: Warm fluid expands, so its density falls and the cooler, denser fluid sinks underneath it - that loop is convection. Radiation plays no part inside the tank, and warming never makes the water heavier.
questions.prompt: Water is heated from below in a tank. Why does the warmed water rise?

questions.answer: The pressure grows by a factor of 450 / 300 = 1.5, because at fixed volume p is proportional to the kelvin temperature: hotter molecules collide with the walls harder and more often.
questions.feedback: A strong answer uses kelvin and the ratio 450/300 = 1.5. If you used degrees Celsius or said the pressure is unchanged, go back to p proportional to T for a fixed volume.
questions.prompt: A sealed gas at 300 K is heated to 450 K at fixed volume. By what factor does its pressure change, and why?
